components.cost_effect: One subgradient query plus one exact prox solve per update; no additional oracle call is implied by the analytical identity.
components.goal: Use ψ to encode the feasible-set geometry in a subgradient update.
components.key_estimate: The associated finite-horizon estimate is recorded separately in thm.P004.weighted_bound; no rate is asserted by the update alone.
components.name: Exact Bregman projection of a linearized objective
components.operation: Query g_k and solve the exact strongly convex subproblem in variant selected.
components.requires: Finite Bregman terms, positive t_k, attained minimizer and a defined gradient at subsequent iterates.
transfer_checks: Re-establish prox solvability and interior preservation after changing X or ψ.
Recompute σ and the dual norm after changing geometry.
An inexact prox or noisy oracle needs an additional error analysis.

limitations.statement: This is a selected exact-update algorithm. Its performance is not an unrestricted Oracle Complexity claim, and exact prox computation may dominate cost.
No Theorem 4.2 anytime rate, boundary-iterate extension, stochastic extension or inexact-prox guarantee is included.

variants.cost: K updates require K subgradient queries and K exact Bregman subproblem solves. Evaluating ψ, ∇ψ, representing X and performing arithmetic inside those solves are additional computational resources, without a source-established universal runtime bound. Optional best-iterate selection requires up to K value queries if values are not bundled with subgradients, K−1 comparisons, and either stored iterates or an online incumbent. Prox solves are not charged as free subgradient calls.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Printed p.170 / PDF p.4, (3.10)–(3.12); Assumption A on printed p.167.
variants.name: SANP with interior iterates
variants.output: The source algorithm generates a sequence. For a finite-horizon interface retain x1,…,x_{K+1}. The associated bound concerns min_{1≤s≤K} f(x_s), not f(x_{K+1}). Optionally query the K function values and return any x_j with j∈argmin_{1≤s≤K}f(x_s); this value-based selection is an explicitly added interface for realizing the source metric.
public_inputs: Closed convex X⊂R^n with int X nonempty; fixed norm; finite-valued strongly convex ψ and its gradient on int X.
Initial x1∈int X, arbitrary positive steps t_k, and optional caller-chosen finite horizon K.
Exact subgradient access and an exact solver for the stated Bregman subproblem.
variants.query_and_update: At k query g_k∈∂f(x_k). Define Bψ(u,v)=ψ(u)−ψ(v)−<∇ψ(v),u−v>. Compute x_{k+1}=argmin_{x∈X}{<g_k,x>+Bψ(x,x_k)/t_k}, equivalently argmin_{x∈X}{t_k<g_k,x>+Bψ(x,x_k)}. This is the exact update in (3.11); no inexact-prox tolerance is included.
variants.requirements: Assumption A: X closed convex with nonempty interior; f:X→R convex and L_f-Lipschitz for the fixed norm; argmin_X f nonempty; computable g∈∂f(x). ψ:X→R is σ-strongly convex for σ>0 and C1 on int X. Exact attained updates and the interior-iterate condition above are required. Efficient prox computation is a separate implementation capability.
variants.state_and_initialization: Store x1∈int X. Require every exact subproblem to attain its minimum and every generated point needed as the second Bregman argument to remain in int X. This selected regime explicitly assumes that property rather than inferring it merely from interior differentiability.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Each t_k>0 is supplied by the caller. For the finite-horizon interface perform K updates, k=1,…,K. No implementable accuracy-based stopping certificate or Theorem 4.2 tuning is claimed. The weighted-bound record applies to every such positive finite sequence.
